description: GEOX Biostratigraphy MCP Concepts — Sabah Event Anchors. 4 canonical Sabah event anchors declared as MCP concepts with truth classes, confidence levels, and relationships. Per Arif sovereign ruling R3 (PARTIAL HOLD): recast as event ANCHORS not event horizons — anchoring points for correlation, not surfaces claiming isochroneity.
doctrine: Event anchors are calibration points for correlation. They are NOT assumptions of basin-wide synchrony or direct physical surfaces unless proven by multi-witness evidence.

deep_regional_unconformity.name: Deep Regional Unconformity / Sabah Orogeny anchor
deep_regional_unconformity.description: Separates pre-early Middle Miocene compressed deep-marine clastic wedge from post-early Middle Miocene NW-prograding shelf/slope clastic wedge. Marks the transition from accretionary/prism compression to post-collisional progradation.
confidence_drivers: Facies shift from deep marine to shelfal
Regional tectonic context (NW Borneo collision ~16-12 Ma)
failure_modes: Mistaking facies shift for true unconformity
Local structural overprint mimicking regional surface
deep_regional_unconformity.biostrat_signature: Missing NN4-NN5 equivalent zones in some sections. Abrupt shift from bathyal to neritic fauna.
references: Tan & Lamy — tectonic evolution of NW Sabah margin

shallow_regional_unconformity.name: Shallow Regional Unconformity
shallow_regional_unconformity.description: Marks later uplift/erosion and reorganization of the Inboard/Outboard clastic systems. Analogous to the ~10-10.5 Ma Upper Miocene Unconformity in Malay Basin. Separates Groups D/E from C.
failure_modes: May be amalgamated with other unconformities in condensed sections
Province-dependent expression — not everywhere same age
Poor biostrat control in uplifted/eroded sections
shallow_regional_unconformity.biostrat_signature: Missing or condensed NN10-NN11 equivalents. Pollen assemblage shift above unconformity.

slab_breakoff_anchor.name: Slab-breakoff / subduction cessation anchor
slab_breakoff_anchor.description: Geodynamic model explaining tectonic relaxation, possible uplift, magmatism pulse, subsidence change, and stress-field shift after cessation of proto-South China Sea subduction beneath NW Borneo. NOT a mappable surface — a process interpretation that may explain multiple observations.
confidence_drivers: Timing consistent with South China Sea spreading cessation (~16 Ma)
Magmatic pulse in some areas (requires geochemical dating)
Subsidence pattern shift from compression to relaxation
failure_modes: Alternative explanations (change in plate boundary, far-field stress)
No direct geophysical evidence (tomography, heat flow) for slab detachment
required_evidence_for_upgrade: Geochemical signature of slab melt in dated volcanics
Heat flow anomaly consistent with asthenospheric upwelling
Timing constraints from thermochronology (AFT, AHe, ZHe)
slab_breakoff_anchor.note: This is the most speculative of the 4 anchors. Per R5 governing principle: remains MODEL_HYPOTHESIS until independently supported by geochemistry, geophysics, and thermochronology.

cob_transition.name: COB transition / South China Sea margin inheritance anchor
cob_transition.description: Continent-Ocean Boundary transition zone beneath NW Sabah. Controls subsidence, heat flow, fault style, basin architecture, and play risk. NOT a line — a ~50 km transition zone of stretched continental crust, hyperextended crust, possible exhumed mantle, volcanic additions, and oceanic crust.
confidence_drivers: Subsidence patterns consistent with stretched continental margin
failure_modes: COB position varies by method (gravity, magnetics, seismic refraction)
Transform segmentation creates abrupt boundaries in some segments
Volcanic overprint may mask transitional crust
~50 km envelope is a working assumption — may be narrower or wider
required_evidence_for_upgrade: Deep seismic refraction/reflection across the margin
Gravity/magnetic forward model with crustal thickness constraints
Basement sample geochemistry from wells penetrating transitional crust
Heat flow measurements across the transition
cob_transition.envelope_note: 50 km is a working uncertainty envelope, not a universal constant. May be narrower where transform margin segments dominate.
play_implications: Heat flow varies across COB — affects maturation timing
Fault style changes from extensional (continental) to possibly different mechanisms at transition
Source rock burial depth may increase abruptly oceanward
Volcanic risk higher in transition zone
references: Huang et al. (2021) — OCT template for South China Sea margins

constitutional_alignment.R3_scoped_wording: These are event ANCHORS — calibration points. NOT event HORIZONS — surfaces claiming isochroneity.
constitutional_alignment.R5_layang_layang: Slab-breakoff anchor remains MODEL_DYNAMIC pending independent geochemical/geophysical/thermochronological evidence.
constitutional_alignment.R6_cob_zone: COB transition modelled as ~50 km zone per ratified R6. Working envelope, not fixed law.
constitutional_alignment.F2_TRUTH: Every anchor carries truth class, confidence, and failure modes.
constitutional_alignment.F6_MARUAH: Process models (slab-breakoff) clearly distinguished from observations (unconformities).
